claim: Peripheral neurons share the capability to switch to a pro-regenerative state after nerve injury.
source: Peripheral neurons are heterogeneous and functionally diverse, but all share the capability to switch to a pro-regenerative state after nerve injury.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general property of peripheral neurons.

claim: Nociceptors showed the greater regeneration after a sciatic crush, followed by motoneurons, mechanoreceptors, and proprioceptors.
source: Using Cre/Ai9 mice that allow fluorescent labeling of neuronal subtypes, we found that nociceptors showed the greater regeneration after a sciatic crush, followed by motoneurons, mechanoreceptors, and, finally, proprioceptors.
evidence: This finding is based on experimental data from Cre/Ai9 mice with fluorescent labeling and axon counting after sciatic nerve crush.

claim: Only 20% of the regulated genes were common among the four neuronal subtypes after axotomy.
source: Only 20% of the regulated genes were common, revealing a diverse response to injury among neurons, which was also supported by the differential influence of neurotrophins among neuron subtypes.
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing data comparing differentially expressed genes across neuronal subtypes.

claim: MED12 is proposed as a specific regulator of the regeneration of proprioceptors.
source: Among differentially regulated genes, we proposed MED12 as a specific regulator of the regeneration of proprioceptors.
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing data showing differential expression of Med12 and functional validation through siRNA knockdown experiments.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing analyses have distinguished up to 11 subtypes in dorsal root ganglia (DRGs).
source: Moreover, peripheral sensory neurons have a wide range of functions and target organs, and single-cell RNA-sequencing analyses have distinguished up to 11 subtypes in dorsal root ganglia (DRGs) (Usoskin et al., 2015; Renthal et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sensory neurons regenerate faster than motoneurons.
source: The finding that sensory neurons regenerate faster than motoneurons has robust evidence (Dolenc and Janko, 1976; Madorsky et al., 1998; Suzuki et al., 1998; Kawasaki et al., 2000; Negredo et al., 2004; Brushart et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Unmyelinated fibers have been described to recover their function earlier than myelinated fibers.
source: In addition, unmyelinated fibers have been described to recover their function earlier than myelinated fibers (Navarro et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Myelinated fibers regenerate at the same speed as unmyelinated fibers.
source: In contrast, alternative work suggests that myelinated fibers regenerate at the same speed as unmyelinated fibers (Lozeron et al., 2004; Moldovan et al., 2006) or even that motoneurons regenerate better than sensory neurons (da Silva et al., 1985).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies that present contrasting findings.

claim: Peripheral neurons activate the Ras/Raf/MAPK pathway after axotomy.
source: After axotomy, peripheral neurons activate several signaling mechanisms such as the Ras/Raf/MAPK pathway (Sheu et al., 2000; Obata et al., 2003; Agthong et al., 2006), the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (Akt) pathway (Kimpinski and Mearow, 2001; Murashov et al., 2001; Edström and Ekström, 2003), the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK)/c-Jun pathway (Kenney and Kocsis, 1998), or the cAMP/protein kinase A/cAMP responsive element binding protein pathway (Gao et al., 2004; Chierzi et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Medium-to-large DRG neurons show an increased activation of extracellular signal-regulated protein kinase compared to small DRG neurons.
source: For instance, medium-to-large DRG neurons show an increased activation of extracellular signal-regulated protein kinase compared to small DRG neurons (Obata et al., 2003; Obata et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inhibition of the RhoA/Rho-kinase pathway enhances motor but not sensory axon regeneration.
source: Importantly, the RhoA/Rho-kinase pathway may have a different role in motor and sensory regeneration given evidence that its inhibition enhances motor but not sensory axon regeneration (Joshi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: TRPV1-Cre/Ai9 mice label mostly peptidergic (42.8 ± 1.2% co-labeling with CGRP) and non-peptidergic (30.1 ± 1.4% IB4-reactive) small-diameter neurons in the DRG.
source: We corroborated that the labeled neurons in the DRG were mostly peptidergic (42.8 ± 1.2% co-labeling with CGRP) and non-peptidergic (30.1 ± 1.4% IB4-reactive) small-diameter neurons.
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence data from TRPV1-Cre/Ai9 mice.

claim: Nociceptors and mechanoreceptors were the populations with the most abundant axons in control nerves.
source: In control nerves, we found that nociceptors and mechanoreceptors were the populations with the most abundant axons, followed by proprioceptors and motoneurons.
evidence: This is based on axon counting data from control nerves in Cre/Ai9 mice.

claim: Seven days after injury, motoneurons and nociceptors achieved axon regrowth similar to controls at 12 mm from the injury site.
source: Seven days after the injury, the number of regenerated axons of the different subpopulation did not reach control values when assessed at a distance of 17 mm from injury site (Figure 1C). However, motoneurons and nociceptors achieved axon regrowth similar to controls at 12 mm from the injury site (Figure 1C, p>0.05 vs their control).
evidence: This is based on axon counting data at 7 days post-injury shown in Figure 1C.

claim: By 9 days after crush, all axon populations had regenerated to numbers comparable to uninjured controls at 12 mm.
source: In contrast, by 9 days after crush, we found that all axon populations had regenerated to numbers comparable to uninjured controls at 12 mm, and only motoneuron and nociceptor axons reached control values at 17 mm (Figure 1C, p>0.05 vs their control).
evidence: This is based on axon counting data at 9 days post-injury shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Motoneurons regrew significantly more axons at 12 mm 9 days after the injury than in control conditions (p=0.038).
source: Motoneurons regrew significantly more axons at 12 mm 9 days after the injury than in control conditions (p=0.038), probably due to the collateral branching at the regenerative front, whereas nociceptors displayed an increase in axon number reaching a plateau at control levels.
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of axon counting data.

claim: At 17 mm and 7 days postinjury, the relative number of regenerated motor axons was significantly lower than that of nociceptors (p=0.012).
source: At this time and distance, the relative number of regenerated motor axons was significantly lower than that of nociceptors (p=0.012), indicating that nociceptors were the population with a greater axonal regeneration (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of relative axon regeneration data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In DRG explants in vitro, nociceptors extended significantly longer neurites than other sensory neurons.
source: This pattern was maintained in DRG explants in vitro, where nociceptors extended significantly longer neurites than other sensory neurons and proprioceptors were the population with shorter neurites (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on neurite length measurements in DRG explant cultures shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Proprioceptors were the population with shorter neurites in DRG explants in vitro.
source: This pattern was maintained in DRG explants in vitro, where nociceptors extended significantly longer neurites than other sensory neurons and proprioceptors were the population with shorter neurites (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on neurite length measurements in DRG explant cultures shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cre/Ribotag mice showed expression of the hemagglutinin (HA) ribosomal tag in neurons in the DRG or spinal cord.
source: These animals showed the expression of the hemagglutinin (HA) ribosomal tag in neurons either in the DRG (co-labeling with β-tubulin) or the spinal cord (co-labeling with ChAT), with a similar pattern to their Cre/Ai9 counterparts (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: RT-qPCR from immunoprecipitates showed a several-fold enrichment of the cell type-specific transcripts Chat, Pvalb, Npy2r, and Trpv1 in their respective IPs.
source: After RNA isolation, RT-qPCR from immunoprecipitates (IPs) showed a several-fold enrichment of the cell type-specific transcripts Chat, Pvalb, Npy2r, and Trpv1 in their respective IPs (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The glial transcript Fabp7 was depleted in all immunoprecipitates.
source: In contrast, the glial transcript Fabp7 (fatty acid binding protein 7) was depleted in all IPs, indicating that the ribosome isolation was neuron-specific.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data showing depletion of Fabp7 in IPs.

claim: The expression of the transcripts Gap43, Atf3, Tubb2b, and Stm2 is enriched in the immunoprecipitates from injured mice compared to control mice in all populations.
source: Among IPs, we saw an enrichment of the transcripts for the regeneration markers Gap43, Atf3, Tubb2b, and Stm2 in lesioned neurons compared to controls in all neuron types (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing data showing transcripts per million (TPM) values in Figure 2E.

claim: A total of 3546, 4053, 3461, and 3281 genes were significantly differentially expressed in motoneurons, proprioceptors, mechanoreceptors, and nociceptors, respectively, 7 days after injury.
source: Compared to intact mice, a total of 3546, 4053, 3461, and 3281 were significantly differentially expressed in datasets from motoneurons, proprioceptors, mechanoreceptors, and nociceptors, respectively, 7 days after injury (Supplementary file 2, Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing differential expression analysis.

claim: Ngfr (p75NTR) was specifically enriched in lesioned motoneurons.
source: For instance, we found that Ngfr (p75NTR), a neurotrophin receptor, was specifically enriched in lesioned motoneurons. This upregulation was confirmed by immunohistochemistry (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing data and confirmed by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Proprioceptors were the only population significantly upregulating Nrp1 and Nrp2 after injury.
source: On the other hand, proprioceptors were the only population significantly upregulating Nrp1 and Nrp2 after injury, which are cell surface receptors for class 3 semaphorins.
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing differential expression analysis.

claim: Increased number of ATF2 positive nuclei were observed by immunohistochemistry in cutaneous mechanoreceptor neurons after injury.
source: Increased number of ATF2 positive nuclei were also observed by immunohistochemistry in cutaneous mechanoreceptor neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: In cutaneous neurons, 20 genes with a log2 fold-change above |2| were not changed in muscle neurons or were regulated in the opposite direction.
source: In cutaneous neurons, we found 20 genes with a log2 fold-change above |2| that were not changed in muscle neurons or were regulated in the opposite direction in both groups (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing differential expression analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Only 2 genes (Med12 and Cacna1b) were downregulated in cutaneous neurons with a log2 fold-change above |2| that were not changed in muscle neurons.
source: Interestingly, only 2 of these genes were downregulated in cutaneous neurons: Med12 and Cacna1b.
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing differential expression analysis.

claim: In muscle neurons, 15 DEGs with a fold-change above |2| were not changed in cutaneous neurons.
source: In muscle neurons, we found 15 DEGs with a fold-change above |2| that were not changed in cutaneous neurons (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing differential expression analysis shown in Figure 3H.

claim: All neurons activate common pathways such as focal adhesion, MAPK, and cAMP signaling pathways after injury.
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis showed that all neurons activate common pathways such as focal adhesion, MAPK, and cAMP signaling pathways (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on KEGG pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Muscle neurons (motoneurons and proprioceptors) significantly regulated the ErbB and VEGF signaling pathways.
source: Muscle neurons (motoneurons and proprioceptors) significantly regulated the ErbB and VEGF signaling pathways, which are potentially relevant for regeneration (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on KEGG pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: GO analysis revealed a specific enrichment of the semaphorin-plexin pathway in muscle neurons (motoneurons and proprioceptors).
source: Importantly, GO analysis revealed a specific enrichment of the semaphorin-plexin pathway in these two neuron subtypes, a crucial pathway in neuron guidance during development and regeneration (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on Gene Ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Cutaneous neurons showed a specific enrichment in cyclic guanosine monophosphate-dependent protein kinase (PKG) and aldosterone signaling pathways.
source: Cutaneous neurons showed a specific enrichment in cyclic guanosine monophosphate-dependent protein kinase (PKG) and aldosterone signaling pathways (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: JNK pathway was found enriched only in nociceptors.
source: JNK pathway, which has been associated to neuropathic pain, was found enriched only in nociceptors (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is based on pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: 10 ng/mL NGF produced the larger increase in neurite length in DRG explants, with a mean longest neurite of 927.5±85.0 µm (p<0.0001 vs control 441.7±32.0 µm).
source: We found that 10 ng/mL NGF produced the larger increase in neurite length, being the mean longest neurite of 927.5±85.0 µm (p<0.0001 vs control 441.7±32.0 µm).
evidence: This is based on neurite length measurements in DRG explants treated with NGF.

claim: 10 ng/mL BDNF significantly increased neurite length in DRG explants (771.1±54.8 µm, p<0.0001).
source: We also observed a significant increase in neurite length with 10 ng/mL BDNF (771.1±54.8 µm, p<0.0001) and 10 ng/mL NT-3 (64.0±48.6 µm, p=0.044).
evidence: This is based on neurite length measurements in DRG explants treated with BDNF.

claim: 10 ng/mL NT-3 significantly increased neurite length in DRG explants (64.0±48.6 µm, p=0.044).
source: We also observed a significant increase in neurite length with 10 ng/mL BDNF (771.1±54.8 µm, p<0.0001) and 10 ng/mL NT-3 (64.0±48.6 µm, p=0.044).
evidence: This is based on neurite length measurements in DRG explants treated with NT-3.

claim: The neurite length of proprioceptors was only significantly increased when adding NT-3 (282.8±57.5 µm vs control 121.8±10.1 µm, p=0.011).
source: The neurite length of proprioceptors was only significantly increased when adding NT-3 (282.8±57.5 µm vs control 121.8±10.1 µm, p=0.011), but not NGF or BDNF (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on neurite length measurements in proprioceptor explants shown in Figure 5B.

claim: NGF and BDNF significantly increased the neurite length of nociceptors (973.5±63.8 µm, p<0.0001 for NGF; 780.1±54.4 µm, p=0.002 for BDNF, both vs control 479.2±45.2 µm).
source: Contrarily, both NGF and BDNF significantly increased the neurite length of nociceptors (973.5±63.8 µm, p<0.0001 for NGF; 780.1±54.4 µm, p=0.002 for BDNF, both vs control 479.2±45.2 µm) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on neurite length measurements in nociceptor explants shown in Figure 5D.

claim: NGF increased neurite length 1.69-fold in mechanoreceptors and 2.03-fold in nociceptors, which was significantly higher than in proprioceptors (0.45-fold change, p=0.007 vs mechanoreceptors; p<0.0001 vs nociceptors).
source: The most specific growth factor for cutaneous neurons was NGF, which increased neurite length 1.69-fold in mechanoreceptors and 2.03-fold in nociceptors. In both cases, this increase was significantly higher than in proprioceptors, which showed a 0.45-fold change (p=0.007 vs mechanoreceptors; p<0.0001 vs nociceptors).
evidence: This is based on normalized neurite length data comparing the effects of NGF across neuronal subtypes.

claim: Proprioceptors showed a 2.32-fold increase in neurite length with NT-3 in opposition to mechanoreceptors (0.8-fold change, p=0.002) and nociceptors (1.13-fold change, p<0.0001).
source: In contrast, the most specific factor for muscle sensory neurons was NT-3. Proprioceptors showed a 2.32-fold increase in neurite length in opposition to mechanoreceptors (0.8-fold change, p=0.002) and nociceptors (1.13-fold change, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is based on normalized neurite length data comparing the effects of NT-3 across neuronal subtypes.

claim: Med12 was upregulated in proprioceptors (20.1 log2 fold-change) and downregulated in mechanoreceptors and nociceptors (–21.0 and –21.6 log2 fold change, respectively) after injury.
source: Results of the RNA-sequencing showed that expression of Med12 was upregulated in proprioceptors (20.1 log2 fold-change) and downregulated in mechanoreceptors and nociceptors (–21.0 and –21.6 log2 fold change, respectively) after injury.
evidence: This is based on RNA-sequencing differential expression analysis.

claim: In cancer cell lines, Med12 has been described to inhibit TGF-β signaling.
source: In cancer cell lines, Med12 has been described to inhibit TGF-β signaling (Huang et al., 2012), an important pathway implicated in regeneration.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Med12 was significantly downregulated using siRNA, with a 57% decrease compared to the scrambled siRNA condition (p=0.001).
source: We found that Med12 was significantly downregulated using this approach (p=0.001), with a 57% decrease compared to the scrambled siRNA condition (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data from siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The longest neurite and the total neurite extension per neuron in proprioceptors were significantly increased in the Med12 knockdown group (p=0.039 and p=0.014, respectively).
source: We found that the longest neurite and the total neurite extension per neuron were significantly increased in the knockdown group (p=0.039 and p=0.014, respectively).
evidence: This is based on neurite length measurements in proprioceptor cultures with Med12 knockdown.

claim: Med12 knockdown did not significantly change neurite length in non-proprioceptive neurons (PV-) labeled with βIII-tubulin.
source: To ensure that this effect was neuron type-specific, we analyzed neurite extension in non-proprioceptive neurons (PV-) labeled with βIII-tubulin. We did not find a significant change in the length of the longest neurite nor in total neuron extension, thus suggesting that MED12 specifically regulated proprioceptive neurite extension.
evidence: This is based on neurite length measurements in non-proprioceptive neurons with Med12 knockdown.

claim: NT-3 has been described as a 'muscle factor' because of its trophic effect on proprioceptors and motoneurons.
source: NT-3 has been described as a 'muscle factor' because of its trophic effect on proprioceptors and motoneurons (Ernfors et al., 1995; Braun et al., 1996; Genç et al., 2004; Taylor et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: NGF has been shown to act specifically on a subpopulation of small primary sensory neurons and on sympathetic neurons.
source: In fact, NGF has been shown to act specifically on a subpopulation of small primary sensory neurons and on sympathetic neurons (Levi-Montalcini, 1987), and later studies confirmed that this factor increased sensory neurites, but not motor neurites (Allodi et al., 2013; Santos et al., 2016b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: MED12 is a subunit of Mediator, a multiprotein complex that regulates transcriptional activity.
source: MED12 is a subunit of Mediator, a multiprotein complex that regulates transcriptional activity (Ding et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Cytoplasmic MED12 was described to inhibit TGF-β receptor 2 through a physical interaction.
source: Besides its known involvement in genomic signaling, cytoplasmic MED12 was described to inhibit TGF-β receptor 2 through a physical interaction (Huang et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The TGF-β pathway is a positive regulator of regeneration since it contributes to the activation of the intrinsic growth capacity of neurons.
source: The TGF-β pathway is a positive regulator of regeneration since it contributes to the activation of the intrinsic growth capacity of neurons (Walshe et al., 2011; Ye et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Bcam encodes a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily that binds to laminin.
source: Muscle neurons strongly upregulated Bcam and Myadm, among other genes. Bcam encodes a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily that binds to laminin (Udani et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: MYADM has been described to be associated with lipid rafts.
source: MYADM has been described to be associated with lipid rafts (Capkovic et al., 2008; Aranda et al., 2013), which are membrane domains involved in growth factor signal transduction, axon guidance, and cellular adhesion (Tsui-Pierchala et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In HeLa and PC3 cell cultures, MYADM is crucial for targeting RAC1 to lipid rafts, facilitating cell migration.
source: In HeLa and PC3 cell cultures, MYADM is crucial for targeting RAC1 to these membrane rafts, facilitating cell migration (Aranda et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In N2a cells, the interaction of GPC2 with midkine was shown to promote cell adhesion and neurite outgrowth.
source: In N2a cells, the interaction of GPC2 with midkine (Sorrelle et al., 2017) was shown to promote cell adhesion and neurite outgrowth (Kurosawa et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ngfr (p75NTR) was found upregulated in previous motoneuron-specific RNA-sequencing.
source: Among the top motoneuron-specific upregulated genes we found Ngfr (p75NTR), which was also found upregulated in previous motoneuron-specific RNA-sequencing (Shadrach et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The activation of p75NTR by neurotrophins can have opposite effects, including both survival and apoptosis.
source: The functions of p75NTR are complex and diverse since its activation by neurotrophins can have opposite effects, including both survival and apoptosis (Roux and Barker, 2002; Chao, 2003; Gutierrez and Davies, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: NRP2 is a cell surface receptor for class 3 semaphorins, with high affinity to SEMA3C and SEMA3F.
source: NRP2 is a cell surface receptor for class 3 semaphorins, with high affinity to SEMA3C and SEMA3F (Chen et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: NRP2 participates in axon guidance during development.
source: This receptor participates in axon guidance during development (Giger et al., 2000; Gil and Del Río, 2019), but its role in peripheral nerve injuries is largely unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Semaphorins are expressed in the nerve after an injury.
source: Semaphorins are expressed in the nerve after an injury (Ara et al., 2004), and their repulsive effect through NRP2 could partially account for impaired growth in proprioceptive axons.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: NDEL1 is a cytoskeleton integrator that participates in the formation of the vimentin-dynein complex during neurite extension.
source: NDEL1 is a cytoskeleton integrator that participates in the formation of the vimentin-dynein complex during neurite extension (Shim et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In vivo silencing of Ndel1 after nerve injury resulted in reduced regeneration.
source: In vivo silencing of Ndel1 after nerve injury resulted in reduced regeneration (Toth et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Upregulation of Atf2 in small and medium DRG neurons was previously reported after injury.
source: We found a significant upregulation of Atf2 in mechanoreceptors. Upregulation of this factor in small and medium DRG neurons was previously reported after injury, and its knockdown reduced tactile allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia after spinal nerve ligation (Salinas-Abarca et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Knockdown of Atf2 reduced tactile allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia after spinal nerve ligation.
source: Upregulation of this factor in small and medium DRG neurons was previously reported after injury, and its knockdown reduced tactile allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia after spinal nerve ligation (Salinas-Abarca et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In neuropathic pain models, the proinflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 (IL-6) is involved in hyperalgesia.
source: In neuropathic pain models, the proinflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 (IL-6) is involved in hyperalgesia (Cunha et al., 1992; Murphy et al., 1999b; Arruda et al., 2000; Melemedjian et al., 2010; Quarta et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Some studies support that IL-6 is involved in the pro-regenerative response of sensory neurons.
source: Furthermore, some studies support that IL-6 is involved in the pro-regenerative response of sensory neurons (Hirota et al., 1996; Murphy et al., 1999a; Murphy et al., 2000; Cafferty et al., 2004; Cao et al., 2006; Zorina et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The intrinsic regenerative capacity differs between peripheral neuron subtypes.
source: Altogether, we demonstrate that the intrinsic regenerative capacity differs between peripheral neuron subtypes, opening the door to selectively modulate these responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Sensory regeneration is inversely proportional to the fiber size: large, myelinated neurons regenerate less robustly than smaller and less myelinated neurons.
source: Altogether these results indicate that sensory regeneration is inversely proportional to the fiber size: large, myelinated neurons regenerate less robustly than smaller and less myelinated neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on regeneration rates of different neuronal subtypes.

claim: Despite their large fiber size, motoneuron regeneration exceeds large-size DRG neurons but not small-size sensory neurons.
source: As for motoneurons, our results suggest that, despite their large fiber size, their regeneration exceeds large-size DRG neurons but not small-size sensory neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on motoneuron regeneration.

claim: MED12 is a novel regulator of neuron-specific regeneration.
source: Altogether, our data demonstrates that MED12 is a novel regulator of neuron-specific regeneration and can be a promising factor to improve proprioceptive regeneration after nerve injury.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Med12 knockdown experiments showing specific effects on proprioceptor neurite extension.

claim: Motoneurons and nociceptors were the populations that recovered their number of axons earlier after sciatic nerve crush.
source: Therefore, motoneurons and nociceptors were the populations that recovered their number of axons earlier.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the axon counting data at different time points and distances.

claim: Motoneurons showed collateral branching at the regenerative front.
source: Motoneurons regrew significantly more axons at 12 mm 9 days after the injury than in control conditions (p=0.038), probably due to the collateral branching at the regenerative front, whereas nociceptors displayed an increase in axon number reaching a plateau at control levels.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that motoneurons had more axons than controls at 12 mm.

claim: The upregulation of MED12 in proprioceptors could hinder axon regeneration through inhibition of TGF-β receptor 2.
source: Knowing MED12's involvement in the TGF-β pathway, we hypothesized that the upregulation of this protein could hinder axon regeneration in proprioceptors through inhibition of TGF-β receptor 2.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on known functions of MED12 and the TGF-β pathway.

claim: The high expression of Il6ra in nociceptors could be one of the contributing mechanisms to the greater regeneration of these neurons after nerve injury.
source: Thus, the high expression of Il6ra in nociceptors could be one of the contributing mechanisms to the greater regeneration of these neurons after nerve injury.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed upregulation of Il6ra and known functions of IL-6.

claim: The lack of upregulation of Ndel1 in proprioceptors is in agreement with the limited regeneration observed in this population after a nerve injury.
source: Thus, the lack of upregulation of Ndel1 in proprioceptors is in agreement with the limited regeneration observed in this population after a nerve injury.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the lack of Ndel1 upregulation to the observed regeneration phenotype.

claim: The repulsive effect of semaphorins through NRP2 could partially account for impaired growth in proprioceptive axons.
source: Semaphorins are expressed in the nerve after an injury (Ara et al., 2004), and their repulsive effect through NRP2 could partially account for impaired growth in proprioceptive axons.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the upregulation of Nrp2 in proprioceptors and known functions of semaphorins.

claim: An overall trophic effect of NT-3 in sensory neurons is largely accounted for by neurite growth from proprioceptors.
source: Here, we confirmed that an overall trophic effect of NT-3 in sensory neurons is largely accounted for by neurite growth from proprioceptors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the neurite outgrowth experiments with NT-3 in different neuronal subtypes.

claim: NGF could be considered a 'cutaneous factor', as it modulates specifically neurite extension of cutaneous neurons but not muscle neurons.
source: Therefore, NGF could be considered a 'cutaneous factor', as it modulates specifically neurite extension of cutaneous neurons but not muscle neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the neurite outgrowth experiments with NGF in different neuronal subtypes.

claim: Neurotrophic factors can be used to modulate differentially muscle and cutaneous sensory neurons.
source: Thus, neurotrophic factors can be used to modulate differentially muscle and cutaneous sensory neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential effects of neurotrophic factors on different neuronal subtypes.

claim: Unmyelinated Npy2r+ fibers may regenerate faster than motoneurons, but this might be masked by the motor regenerative collaterals and the heterogeneity in Npy2r+ neurons.
source: Since our cutaneous mechanoreceptors include myelinated and unmyelinated fibers, a more variable regeneration rate can be expected in these animals. We speculate that unmyelinated Npy2r+ fibers may regenerate faster than motoneurons, but this might be masked by the motor regenerative collaterals and the heterogeneity in Npy2r+ neurons.
evidence: This is a speculation to explain the observed regeneration patterns.

claim: Axotomy might trigger the expression of regeneration inhibitory factors in proprioceptors that slows this process.
source: Since the regeneration of proprioceptors is limited, we thought that axotomy might trigger the expression of regeneration inhibitory factors in this population that slows this process.
evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain the limited regeneration of proprioceptors.
